summary: Edward Upham (1776–1834) worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He served as a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London and was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society from circa 1824 to 1834.

Edward Vernon Arnold (1857–1926) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his B.A. and Litt.D. at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell, studied at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and was a professor at Bangor University from 1884 to 1924.
Edward W. Said (1935–2003) studied at Princeton and Harvard University. He served on the faculty at Columbia University in English and Comparative Literature from circa 1963 until 2003.

Edward Washburn Hopkins (1857–1932) studied at Columbia and earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, having also studied under Albrecht Weber. An Indologist and linguist, he taught at Bryn Mawr (1885–1895) and Yale (1895–1926).
Edward William West (1824–1905) worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at King's College London, under Duncan Forbes, and later under Martin Haug between 1867 and 1873.

Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, also studying under Geshe Lobsang, Geshe Lobsang Donyo, and Lobsang Tenzin.

Edward Winter Clark (1830–1913) worked in linguistics. He studied at Brown University, Newton Theological Institution, and Colgate Rochester Crozer Divinity School, later serving as a missionary with the American Baptist Missionary Union from 1869 to 1911.

Edwin Abbott Abbott (1838–1926) studied at City of London School and St John's College. He held teaching posts at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and Clifton College, before serving at the City of London School from 1865 to 1889.

Edwin Arnold (1832–1904) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology. Educated at King's College London and Oxford (B.A. 1854), he served as principal of Deccan College from 1856 to 1861 and founded the Maha Bodhi Society.

Edwin Capers Kirkland (1902–1972) was a scholar of Indology who earned his Ph.D. from Northwestern University. He held posts at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (circa 1934–1946) and the University of Florida, where he was Professor of English in 1946.

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson (1840–1890) was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Trinity College Dublin. He served as president of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (circa 1888–1890).

Edwin Francis Bryant (born 1957) is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University, taught at Harvard University from circa 1998 to 2001, and became Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University circa 2003.

Edwin Gerow (1931–2023) worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under George V. Bobrinskoy, J. A. B. van Buitenen, Louis Renou, and V. Ranganathan. He held posts at the University of Washington and Reed College.

Edwin Greaves (1854–1941) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Western College. He served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society (circa 1881–1918) and was principal of its college in Benares and the Missionary Language School in Lucknow.

Edwin Hotchkiss Tuttle (1879–1939) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale University from circa 1897 to 1901. He later worked as a language teacher at the Mackenzie School and the Boys' Latin School of Maryland.

Edwin Lee Johnson (1874–1947) studied at the University of Mississippi and Vanderbilt University (Ph.D. 1910). He worked in linguistics and Indology, later serving at Vanderbilt University as an assistant, fellow, and Professor of Latin and Greek (1935).
Edwin Möhrke (died 1960) was an Indologist. He studied philology at the University of Marburg in 1923 and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Königsberg in 1934 under Helmuth von Glasenapp.

Edwin Norris (1795–1872) worked in linguistics, Indology, and history. He served at the East India Company, the Foreign Office, and the Royal Asiatic Society, where he was Assistant Secretary, editor of its journal, and Honorary Librarian.

Edwin Whitfield Fay (1865–1920) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Rhodes College, Johns Hopkins (Ph.D. 1890), and Leipzig. He held professorships at Washington and Lee University and the University of Texas at Austin.

Egaku Maeda (1926–2010) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He was a professor at Aichi Gakuin University (1972–2002).
